propositions: After a single transport failure (TLS, DNS, timeout) during git push, Bridge abandons delivery without retries, leaving converged commits unpushed and silently lost.
The push.py classifier treats all non-zero push outcomes except non-fast-forward as terminal, conflating permanent policy violations with transient transport faults that could succeed on retry.

Transport faults in both the explicit fetch leg (_recover_non_fast_forward) and the on-demand promisor fetch leg (_merge_remote_under_lock during merge under blob:none partial clone) need subtractive classification to distinguish from genuine merge conflicts and policy declines.
The retry budget and backoff strategy must be bounded (3 attempts with 0.5s then 2.0s sleep) to survive transient blips without stalling on real outages.

Reason vocabulary and strict contract must be unchanged: policy declines stay terminal after 1 attempt, merge conflicts stay terminal, and terminal transport failures still raise push-transport-failed with git stderr and unpushed-commit summary.
